# dsh-resend-mcp

Resend email tools for DeepSeek Harness,
wrapped as an installable DSH bundle.

**Home:** <https://git.pvlb.dev/dsh-plugins/dsh-resend-mcp> ·
**Mirror:** <https://github.com/pvlb-d

ev/dsh-resend-mcp> ·
**Listing:** <https://dsh-plugin.org/plugins/pvlb-dev/dsh-resend-mcp>

The plugin connects to Resend's hosted MCP server
(`https://mcp.resend.com/mcp`), resolves your API

key from the DSH credential
store, and exposes a **curated subset** of Resend's tools as native agen

t tools
named `mcp__resend__<tool>`. A diagnostic `resend_status` tool reports the
connection, crede
ntial reference, and active filter without revealing the key.

2026-10-22 against DSH `0.2.0-rc.2` and Resend's live MCP
server: 9 tools registered from 137 avail

able, and a test email was delivered
from `dsh@pvlb.dev` to `pvlb.dev@gmail.com`. CI runs on Forgejo

Actions;

npmjs and in the Forgejo
registry, and is listed on

## What it looks like

One install command and one credential entry, and the model gets nine
`mcp__resend__*` tools plus a

diagnostic. Real output from `resend_status` on
the reference deployment (DSH `0.2.0-rc.2`, Resend M

the reference deployment (DSH `0.2.0-rc.2`, Resend MCP server `1.2.1`):

The send path is verified end to end: a message sent from `dsh@pvlb.dev`
reported `delivered`, and `

mcp__resend__get-email` returned it by its Resend
ID. `mcp__resend__list-domains` confirms the sendi

ng domain is verified with
sending enabled.
## Why a subset?

Resend's MCP server currently exposes **137 tools** whose JSON schemas total
roughly **405 KB** — on

every model request. Most sessions need a handful of
them. This plugin selects a small, useful pres

et by default and lets you widen
it explicitly:
| Preset | Tools | Approx. schema size |

| `minimal` | `send-email`, `list-emails`, `get-email`, `list-domains` | ~13 KB |
| `sending` *(defa
ult)* | minimal + `list-contacts`, `get-contact`, `create-contact`, `list-templates`, `list-broadcas

ts` | ~26 KB |
| `inbox` | minimal + ten inbox read/thread/draft tools | ~54 KB |
| `full` | every t

ool the server exposes | ~405 KB today |
| `custom` | whatever `tools` matches | user-controlled |
## Requirements

- Node.js >= 22.6
- DSH `>=0.2.0-rc.1 <0.3.0`
- A Resend account with a verified sending domain and

an API key
- `pnpm` available to the DSH Plugin Manager (the profile may need to name its
absolute p

PI key
- `pnpm` available to the DSH Plugin Manager (the profile may need to name its
absolute path)

es

## Configure the API key

1. Create a key at <https://resend.com/api-keys> with permission to send email
and read the resource

s you want the agent to use.
2. Add it to the local credential store, `~/.dsh/.credentials.yaml` (or
`$DSH_HOME/.credentials.yaml`), under the existing `refs:` map:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

Add the entry; do not replace `version`, `records`, or other refs. The store
watches the file and re

loads it on change, so no restart is needed.
3. Keep the file owner-only. DSH refuses to load a cred

entials file that group
or others can read; fix it with
`chmod 600 ~/.dsh/.credentials.yaml` if nece

s file that group
or others can read; fix it with
`chmod 600 ~/.dsh/.credentials.yaml` if necessary.

The key is resolved through `ctx.credentials` at connect time and never written
to configuration, lo
gs, tool output, or the repository.

This deployment's Web UI does not expose a generic credential editor, so
editing the file (or export

ing `RESEND_API_KEY` before launching DSH) is the
[该节后续省略]
## Security

- The API key is resolved from DSH credentials at connect/reconnect time.
- Configuration carries on

ly the credential reference, never the value.
- Logs contain counts, names, and error messages — not

headers or secrets.
- `resend_status` reports only whether the credential is configured and from
wh

ich layer (`file`, `env`, …).
- The repository test suite includes a secret scan and fails on accide

, `env`, …).
- The repository test suite includes a secret scan and fails on accidental
`re_…` keys.

The credential store protects against accidental disclosure, not against a
malicious agent running a

s the same OS user; see the DSH credentials
documentation for that boundary.
## Limitations

- Remote Streamable HTTP only; no stdio `resend-mcp` process and no OAuth
browser flow.
- API-key be

arer authentication only.
- DSH validates only its own JSON Schema subset locally. Resend keywords s

uch as
`format`, `pattern`, `minItems`, and `maxItems` reach the model but are
enforced by Resend's

server.
- Reconnection uses bounded exponential backoff; after the attempt budget the
tools are unre

gistered until the plugin reloads or the Host restarts.
- No settings UI yet; configure through YAML

.
- The plugin is installed profile-wide, affecting every session in that profile.
